pages.text: A worn catalyst is choked with coke. Burning it off in air goes faster hotter (k ∝ e^(−Eₐ/RT)) and with more oxygen - but above about 900 K the metal grains merge, and what sinters is lost. Run it where the coke goes and the metal stays.
$(thing)Set$(): Burn-off temperature, Oxygen flow.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Draught: the oxygen reaching the bed varies by ±3%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): none beyond the recipe windows.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): The faster the coke burns, the faster each batch.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Burn rate: k ∝ e^(−Eₐ/R·(1/T − 1/800 K))$(br)Coke removed: C = 1 − e^(−k·f/2)$(br)Sintered: S = 1 − e^(−(T − 900 K)/60 K)$(br)Restored: R = C·(1 − S)
